title: Working from Home: Freedom or Isolation?
essay:
Over the past few years, working from home has become common in many professions. First of all, employees save time and money because they no longer have to travel to the office every day. Indeed, some people say they feel calmer and more productive in their own living room than in a noisy open space. However, not everyone enjoys this new way of working.

For example, a young accountant might spend eight hours alone in front of a screen. Although she gains more flexibility, she may also feel disconnected from her colleagues. Moreover, it can be difficult to separate professional life from personal life when the kitchen table is also the office. Therefore, many remote workers follow a strict schedule and take regular breaks.

Technology helps people stay in touch by offering video calls and instant messages. Thanks to these tools, teams can share ideas quickly, even when they live in different cities. Nevertheless, a screen cannot replace a friendly conversation at the coffee machine. On the other hand, going to the office every day is not always necessary to build trust between coworkers.

In my opinion, employers should offer a mix of home and office days. Flexible schedules and a comfortable workspace would help employees organize their day in order to balance work and family responsibilities. Finally, working from home is neither good nor bad in itself; what matters is how we use it to stay productive, healthy and connected.
